title: FastAPI Examples
description: Each example belongs to one starter lesson. Follow its setup steps before trying it. These examples need the named tools and do not run in this site playground.

examples.title: Return a greeting
examples.description: A route decorator maps GET / to a function. PlainTextResponse makes a plain text reply.
examples.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, HTTPException, Response, status
from fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
app = FastAPI()
@app.get("/", response_class=PlainTextResponse)
def hello():
    return "Hello, Asha!"

examples.title: Return a data object
examples.description: A Python dictionary becomes JSON. Open GET /book.

examples.title: Check a path number
examples.description: The n: int type lets FastAPI parse and check a route input. Open GET /double/4.

examples.title: Supply a query default
examples.description: An input not in the path is read from the query. GET /page with no n uses its default.

examples.title: Limit an input range
examples.description: Query can add rules such as a minimum and maximum. Open GET /page?n=3.

examples.title: Check a JSON body
examples.description: A Pydantic model describes body fields. Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip","pages":24}.

examples.title: Choose returned fields
examples.description: A response model describes the public data. GET /book leaves out the internal note.

examples.title: Report a missing item
examples.description: HTTPException stops normal handling with an error reply. Open GET /missing.
examples.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, HTTPException, Response, status
from fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
app = FastAPI()
@app.get("/missing")
def missing():
    raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Book not found")

examples.title: Add response metadata
examples.description: The Response input lets a function set headers. Open GET /note.

examples.title: Point to another URL
examples.description: RedirectResponse sends a Location header. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello.

examples.title: Return a typed list
examples.description: A list response can contain several small data objects. Open GET /books.

examples.title: Wait without blocking
examples.description: An async route can await an async operation. GET /score waits for a completed coroutine and returns its result.
examples.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, HTTPException, Response, status
from fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse, RedirectResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
app = FastAPI()
async def read_score():
    return 8
@app.get("/score")
async def score():
    value = await read_score()
    return {"score": value}
